21
22   TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
23

24   COMES NOW, Robert Freehill, pro se Intervenor, Party 328 (referred throughout as “Robert
25   Freehill”) respectfully files this Post Hearing on the Merits Initial Brief and shows as follows:

26

27                                         I. INTRODUCTION

28   On March 26, 2026, Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services
29   Corporation (“Applicants”) filed a joint application to amend their Certificates of Convenience
30   and Necessity (“CCNs”) to construct the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV
31   Transmission Line Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason,

                                             Post Hearing on the Merits Initial Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                   SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                       Page 2 of 7


1    McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Willamson Counties
2    (the “Project”).

3    Intervenor Robert Freehill was admitted to the docket as an intervenor1 and has standing and a
4    direct, justiciable interest in this proceeding because Segment F34 is immediately adjacent to
5    Tract 2390, Robert Freehill’s property2; and, as developed in the evidentiary record, the
6    Applicants’ routing analysis for Segment F34 failed to fully consider material community
7    features in the corridor, including an operational elementary school within 500 feet of the
8    proposed segment and a planned highway interchange intersecting the right-of-way. Those
9    omissions are significant because PURA requires consideration of community values, historical
10   and aesthetic values, and other public-interest factors when selecting a transmission route. The
11   evidence further shows that Segment F34 imposes disproportionate impacts on the surrounding
12   residential and community environment and therefore should not be considered.

13                                               II. ARGUMENT

14       A. Florence ISD Elementary School: The Florence ISD Elementary School is located
15           within 500 feet of Segment F343. Despite its proximity, the school was not fully
16           considered during route planning. The evidentiary record establishes that the facility was
17           identified using a habitable structure icon rather than a school icon4. Mr. Marusak further
18           testified that Florence ISD Elementary School is the only school identified within 500
19           feet in Table 75 and Attachment 13 of the Application, as amended5. The significance of
20           this evidence extends beyond a mapping discrepancy. An elementary school is a
21           substantial community resource serving students, families, educators, and the surrounding
22           community. Because the school was not accurately reflected during the routing analysis,
23           the impacts of Segment F34 on community values may not have been fully evaluated.
24           This fact weighs against reliance on Segment F34 when comparing route alternatives that
25           avoid or minimizes impacts to established community facilities. Segment F34 was

                                                                                     PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                        Page 3 of 7


1            evaluated using incomplete information about a major community facility, which
2            undermines confidence that Segment F34 properly satisfies PURA community-values
3            criterion.
4
5        B. Williamson County planned “Corridor J” Highway Interchange at CR138 and
6            SH195: Segment F34 is proposed to run parallel to County Road 138. Evidence in the
7            record demonstrates that Williamson County's planned Corridor J project includes a
8            major highway interchange at the intersection of CR138 and SH1956. In Mr. Kennedy’s
9            cross-examination of Mr. Poole, Mr. Poole testifies that it is good planning to avoid a
10           transportation corridor7. A review of the exhibits indicates that Segment F34 right-of-
11           way and the planned interchange occupy the same general area. In particular, the northern
12           portion of Segment F34 right-of-way appears to overlap or closely coincide with areas
13           planned for the southern lanes and associated on- and off-ramps of the future interchange.
14           Whether or not a direct engineering conflict presently exists, the record establishes that a
15           significant transportation facility is planned immediately adjacent to, and potentially
16           within, the same corridor proposed for Segment F34. This circumstance weighs against
17           selection of F34 because it introduces uncertainty regarding long-term compatibility with
18           planned public infrastructure and suggests that the route was not developed with full
19           consideration of known local transportation planning. When considered together with the
20           Florence ISD Elementary School located within approximately 500 feet of Segment F34,
21           the evidence demonstrates that F34 traverses an area of substantial existing and planned
22           public development. These facts and public-use impacts weigh against Segment F34.
23
24       C. The surrounding residential and community environment: The northern and eastern
25           boundaries of Robert Freehill’s property are adjacent to proposed Segment F34 of the
26           Bell County East Switch – Big Hill 765 kV Transmission Line Project8. Segment F34
27           parallels County Road 230 going north and then turns west just north of the northeast
28           corner of Robert Freehill’s property. Segment F34 then parallels his entire northern fence

       JKK-Poole Ex. 04; Williamson County Ex. A-L
     7
       Transcript, 10JUN26, page 115, lines 2-11
     8
       Direct Testimony of Robert Freehill Exhibit 4 – Tract 2390 and Segment F34.

                                                                                      PUC Docket No. 59475

                                                         Page 4 of 7


1            line 630 feet north of that northern fenceline. At one point, Segment F34’s centerline is
2            790 feet from Robert Freehill’s residence9.
3            1. Evidence of residential/community value impact: The western viewshed is part of
4                 the property's established residential and recreational use. The evidence establishes
5                 that Segment F34 would be located directly within the primary western viewshed
6                 from the residence. The record further shows that the residence, patio, and backyard
7                 areas are regularly used for outdoor residential and recreational activities, including
8                 observation of sunsets, wildlife, and livestock. Consequently, selection of Segment
9                 F34 would substantially alter the visual environment associated with the property's
10                routine use and enjoyment10. Robert Freehill has the unique view of the seasonal
11                movement of the sunsets throughout the year with the endpoints being the winter and
12                summer solstices11. Robert Freehill’s wife regularly spends time outdoors on the
13                property, including in the backyard and patio areas, where we engage in routine
14                residential and recreational activities and observe sunsets, livestock, migratory birds
15                and native wildlife12
16
17           2. Impact on Land Use and Economics: The record establishes that Segment F34
18                would be located immediately upslope from an intermittent stream and two ponds that
19                contribute to the property's agricultural and recreational uses. The evidence further
20                establishes that the terrain generally slopes north to south toward these features 13.
21                The affected area includes the intermittent stream and two ponds that contribute to the
22                property's agricultural and recreational use. Segment F34 could impact Robert
23                Freehill’s pastureland, surface water, and drainage patterns14.
24
25           3. Enjoyment of the Property: Robert Freehill’s property is more than a residence; it
26                is an integrated residential, agricultural, and family-use property. The record

1                    demonstrates that the property serves multiple purposes, including residential
2                    occupancy, agricultural activities, livestock management, family gatherings, wildlife
3                    observation, and outdoor recreation. The visual, agricultural, and environmental
4                    impacts associated with Segment F34 therefore extend beyond a simple aesthetic
5                    concern and affect the overall use and enjoyment of the property as it presently exists.
6                    Segment F34 impacts to the property’s agricultural use and rural character, visual
7                    setting, perceived marketability, and the overall enjoyment Robert Freehill derives
8                    from living on and using the property for residential, family, and agricultural
9                    purposes15
10
11                                                      III. Conclusion
12
13   The record demonstrates that Segment F34 is not consistent with PURA or the Commission’s
14   planning criteria of avoiding the concentration of community, educational, residential, and
15   planned infrastructure impacts present along proposed Segment F34. The Commission need not
16   consider Segment F34. The record shows that Segment F34 was not fully evaluated against
17   existing and planned public infrastructure, residential development, and community values
18   within the affected area. Evidence entered into the record established that the Florence ISD
19   Elementary School is located within approximately 500 feet of Segment F34 and was not
20   properly identified during the route evaluation process. The record further establishes the
21   existence of significant planned transportation infrastructure in the immediate vicinity of
22   Segment F34 that was likewise not fully considered during route development and evaluation.
23   The record also demonstrates substantial impacts to surrounding residential properties and
24   community values. As reflected in Robert Freehill’s testimony and exhibits, Segment F34 would
25   parallel the northern and eastern boundaries of my property for an extended distance, placing
26   approximately 200-foot transmission structures directly within the viewshed of a long-
27   established rural residential and agricultural property. The evidence shows potential impacts to
28   scenic views, enjoyment of property, wildlife habitat, agricultural activities, recreational uses,
29   marketability, and the overall rural character of the area.


     15
          Robert Freehill’s Direct Testimony, page 17, lines 5-8
                                                       Post Hearing on the Merits Initial Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                          PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                             SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                  Page 6 of 7


1    Taken together, the evidence demonstrates that Segment F34 presents significant concerns
2    relating to community values and compatibility with existing and planned land uses. Because
3    important residential, educational, and infrastructure considerations were not fully identified or
4    evaluated during the routing process, the record does not support a conclusion that Segment F34
5    is viable. The Honorable Administrative Law Judges should eliminate the consideration of
6    Segment F34 due to the public interest, surrounding community values, and the routing criteria
7    established by the Public Utility Regulatory Act and Commission rules.
8
